**📅 September 2, 2026**
**📊 Market Sentiment:** Bearish
**🎯 Confidence:** High

**🧠 Key Themes**
• Middle East escalation is driving an oil supply shock, with Brent surging past $90–$94 and tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz threatening sustained disruptions.
• A synchronized global bond rout has pushed Treasury yields to their highest since early 2025, with UK, Japanese, and European borrowing costs also spiking to multi-decade highs.
• Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s hawkish pivot has markets repricing September toward a potential rate hike, crushing the prior easing narrative and pressuring rate-sensitive assets.
• Equities are breaking key technical support, with the Dow dropping 400 points and broad weakness across tech, financials, and energy-sensitive sectors despite isolated AI earnings beats.

**⚠️ Notable Risks**
• Disorderly bond market selloff and potential liquidity stress as global yields spike in tandem.
• Severe supply shock if Hormuz transit is materially disrupted by widening U.S.-Iran hostilities.
• Policy error risk from a Fed hiking into a slowing economy facing energy-driven inflation.

**📈 Volatility Outlook:** Rising

**🧾 One-Line Take**
A stagflationary shock from surging oil and yields, combined with a hawkish Fed pivot and breaking equity technicals, is driving a decisive risk-off regime with expanding volatility into September.
